subject: Computer Networking
title: BGP: The Routing Glue
description: A micro-lesson that makes BGP: The Routing Glue usable.

hook.text: Thousands of independent networks form the internet. BGP is how they tell each other what they can reach.

buildup.text: BGP stands for Border Gateway Protocol. Each network announces its IP ranges to its neighbors.

discovery.text: Routers use BGP announcements to build a map of the internet and choose paths for every packet.

twist.text: A BGP misconfiguration can reroute millions of users through the wrong network. It's happened many times.

climax.text: In 2021, a bad BGP update took Facebook offline for hours. The whole world noticed immediately.

punchline.text: BGP runs on trust. One bad announcement can break the internet.

quiz.question: What is BGP's role in the internet?
options: It lets networks announce reachable routes to each other
It assigns IP addresses to individual users

details.summary: Border Gateway Protocol connects the internet's autonomous systems, which are large networks operated by ISPs, companies, and institutions. BGP routers exchange information about reachable networks and select paths based on policy, not just shortest distance.
details.whyItMatters: BGP is the protocol that holds the internet together. Its policy-based routing reflects business relationships, and BGP errors have caused massive outages.
takeaways: BGP connects autonomous systems across the internet
It uses policy-based path selection, not just shortest path
BGP misconfigurations have caused major internet outages

faq.question: Why is BGP considered fragile?
faq.answer: BGP was designed with implicit trust between operators. Any autonomous system can announce routes to any network, whether legitimate or not. Route hijacking, whether accidental or malicious, can redirect traffic globally. RPKI adds verification but adoption is incomplete.

faq.question: How did a BGP error take down Facebook in 2021?
faq.answer: Facebook accidentally withdrew its own BGP routes during a maintenance operation. Every other network lost the path to Facebook's IP ranges. DNS servers for Facebook became unreachable. The outage lasted six hours because engineers could not access internal tools to fix it.
